source_evidence: A subscription-based fee is a set, recurring fee that you pay for a particular service, typically on a monthly basis.
answer: A subscription-based advisory fee is a recurring set amount—often charged monthly—in exchange for the investment management services described in your agreement. Unlike an asset-based fee, which is calculated as a percentage of your account’s assets and changes in dollar amount as their value changes, a subscription fee does not automatically shrink when your account balance is smaller. For example, a $3 monthly fee totals $36 per year; on a $500 account, that is more than 7% of the account’s value. So when comparing fee structures, consider the annual subscription cost relative to the account balance, as well as what services the adviser provides.
formula_latex: \text{Annual fee as a percentage of account value} = \frac{\text{monthly fee} \times 12}{\text{account balance}} \times 100\%
